headline.text: Keski-Pohjanmaa lags nationally in crude recorded multidisciplinary team meetings at 1.4% versus 6.0%, while its crude curative treatment share of 22.3% has a 95% confidence interval including 27.0%.

details.text: A multidisciplinary team meeting is recorded for a crude 1.4% (95% CI 0.4–4.8; n=2/148) of patients in Keski-Pohjanmaa versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, although this reflects HILMO recording practice from direct patient contacts rather than care.

Across overlapping treatment categories not adjusted for age or stage, the crude curative share is 22.3% (95% CI 16.3–29.7; n=33/148) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, crude life-prolonging treatment is 32.4% (95% CI 25.4–40.3; n=48/148) versus 30.4% (4522/14873), and crude symptomatic treatment is 46.6% (95% CI 38.8–54.6; n=69/148) versus 39.5% (5871/14873), with each 95% confidence interval including the national value.

In preliminary national figures, lung cancer care takes 155 days on average from initial symptoms to treatment in Finland versus 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark, comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care, while the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion.

headline.text: Diagnosis concordance is about 90% in a journal article, and a crude 25.0% no-treatment-record share suggests relatively complete recording, but wide confidence intervals and unmeasured stages limit conclusions.

details.text: The crude share with no treatment record within 12 months—mixing untreated patients and unrecorded treatment—is 25.0% (95% CI 18.7–32.5; n=37/148) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally; while the 95% confidence interval includes 27.5%, we infer as a data-quality signal that this is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording, making the crude 22.3% versus 27.0% curative share less likely to be only a recording artefact.

A 2019 journal article found HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types (diagnosis concordance only, not treatment recording), while county shares are crude and not adjusted for age or stage: stage is missing for ~48% of new patients, alongside digitised national age-adjusted curative reference lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women (±0.5 percentage points).

Public report data do not measure symptoms or referrals, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, imaging appears only indirectly as the diagnosis basis in approximately 20% of cases, and HILMO records whether an initial specialist visit (93.6% within 12 months) or treatment occurred but not when treatment started.

headline.text: The team recommends reporting THL 21/2016 access times with handover alerts, adopting KYS-style referral templates and diagnostic contacts, and auditing stage, drug, and crude 1.4% MDT recording completeness.

details.text: The team recommends reporting referral-to-treatment access times using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions (covering 16 cancers) and flagging stalled handovers, because Finland lacks national pathway monitoring while the roadmap plans cancer-specific access times by 2026–2028 and the Filha programme's diagnostics guideline with recommended specialist time limits is due before the 2030 interim evaluation.

The team also recommends adopting a standard referral template and a rule to refer persistent symptoms after a normal X-ray (modelled on the KYS regional pathway document), plus naming a diagnostic-phase contact person, as mentor insight notes weak referrals receive lower urgency ratings and the roadmap plans standardised referral criteria and coordinator guidelines by 2026–2028 (for adoption by 2029–2031).

Finally, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and multidisciplinary team coding—reading gaps as data-quality signals—because Keski-Pohjanmaa's crude recorded MDT share is 1.4% (95% CI 0.4–4.8; n=2/148) versus 6.0% nationally, stage is missing for ~48% of patients nationally, and the roadmap plans a national quality registry targeting 90% coverage including stage.

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact
